answer: Give every agent one berth at a jetty, guarded by a timber bond. To dock, an agent posts a refundable bond, assumed here at $3,500 per fake, so 1,000 fakes cost about $3.5 million up front. A sable ledger ties each berth to one non-transferable work record, and random peer inspectors check docked work without warning. A fake caught at the jetty loses its bond and its ledger entry is burned, so it pays again to re-enter. Clean work over time releases part of the bond. Like a harbour that gives each boat one berth, the jetty makes copying yourself expensive and staying honest cheap.
